result.text: A university enrollment system involves the following steps: Prospective students submit an application online.
The admissions office reviews the application and supporting documents.
If documents are missing, the applicant is notified to provide the missing items.
Upon receiving all documents, the application is evaluated by the admissions committee.
Concurrently, the finance department processes any application fees or waivers.
If the application is accepted, an acceptance letter is sent.
Otherwise, a rejection letter is sent and the process ends.
After being accepted, the student must then confirm enrollment by a specified deadline; otherwise the application will be canceled.
If the student confirms, they receive orientation materials and the IT department sets up student accounts for email, online portals, and library access.
If the student is international, the international student office assists with visa processing.
The student obtains a student ID card and starts creating their study plan, which includes: Meeting with an academic advisor.
Selecting courses.
Resolving any schedule conflicts.
The student begins attending classes.
Throughout each semester, the student may add or drop courses within the add/drop period.
At the end of the semester, grades are posted, and the student can review them online.
If the student has any grievances, they can file an appeal, which includes: Submitting an appeal form.
Meeting with the appeals committee.
Awaiting a decision.
The process repeats each semester until the student graduates or withdraws.

result.rule: When the description lists two or more activities that are performed without a stated order and must all be completed before a later step begins: Model a parallel gateway that splits into one outgoing branch per listed activity, and a parallel gateway that joins those branches before the next step. Do not chain the activities in sequence, and do not use an exclusive gateway for them.

When the description lists two or more actions that must all be carried out after a common point, with no order or alternative stated between them, and only then leads to a later step: Model a parallel gateway that splits into one task per listed action, keeping each action as its own task with the description's wording, in a separate branch. Join all branches with a parallel gateway before the later step, so the later step waits for every action. Do not chain the actions in sequence, do not use an exclusive gateway for them, and do not leave any branch without a connecting flow to the join.

When the description lists several activities that are performed together with no stated order and must all be finished before a later step, and one of those activities happens only in certain cases, so it is conditional: Model each fixed activity as its own task in a separate branch of a parallel gateway split. Place the conditional activity behind an exclusive gateway inside its own branch, with one outgoing flow for the case where it happens and one for the case where it does not. Join all branches with a parallel gateway before the later step. Do not wrap these activities in an embedded subprocess, and do not chain them in sequence.

When the description lists several activities that must all be finished before the process ends, with no order stated among them, and the end is described as waiting until every one of them is done: Model each listed activity as its own task. Fork them from one parallel gateway, merge them through a second parallel gateway, and place the end event after that join. Do not chain the activities in an arbitrary sequence, and do not let any branch reach the end event before the others have finished.

Use a gateway to route from the cycle to these exit branches. Do not replace an exit action with a bare end event named after its outcome. Keep the cycle's back-edge for the non-exit path.

When the description says a repeated sequence of activities runs each period until the participant reaches one of several named final outcomes: Model an exclusive gateway that returns to the first repeated activity and exits through one task per named final outcome. Each outcome task leads to an end event, so no named outcome is left out of the model.

When the description states a condition that decides whether the process continues to a further outcome or ends, for example 'if all criteria are met, ...' followed by a consequence: Model an exclusive gateway at the point where the condition is decided, with one labeled outgoing sequence flow for each outcome the description states. Place the gateway before the outcome that the condition governs, and do not leave the conditional outcome as an unconditional sequence of tasks.

When the description states that the process ends once a completion step has been carried out successfully, and that a later occurrence (such as feedback or a return) may follow after the end: Model the completion step as its own task on the main flow, placed directly before a single end event. Name the end event for the process end, not for the outcome. Model the later occurrence as a separate task or branch that is joined to the main flow through a gateway, and do not fold it into the label of the end event.
